title: Director Customer to Cash
jobDescription: The Customer to Cash Director will lead the end-to-end Customer to Cash function for the business, ensuring customers can be onboarded, billed, supported, collected from and serviced accurately as Omni's standalone C2C capability comes online. Omni is a newly separated business operating under a Transition Service Agreement (TSA) with its former parent, Thomson Reuters (TR). At Day 1, only Order Entry sits within Omni; Billing, Cash Application, Collections and Master Data continue to be delivered by TR under the TSA. This role will lead the stand-up of standalone C2C capability, progressively bringing each function out of TSA scope and into Omni ownership according to the agreed transition roadmap, with all TSA-covered C2C services fully transitioned before TSA expiry. This is a hands-on leadership role requiring strong people management, operational discipline, customer focus and the ability to learn quickly in a complex environment. The successful candidate will bring clarity to ownership, simplify processes, improve speed and predictability, and build a high-performing team that supports sales, finance, customer experience and regional business leaders. About The Role In this opportunity as Director Customer to Cash, your key responsibilities will be: Operational Leadership Lead the end-to-end Customer to Cash operating model, ensuring timely, accurate and consistent execution across order processing, billing, cash application, collections and master data. Ensure customers are invoiced accurately and on time, with clear ownership of exceptions, adjustments, cancellations, refunds, credits and dispute handling. Oversee order, billing, cash application and collections processes across relevant platforms, including e Store, Salesforce/Conga, SAP, Bill Trust and Esker. Lead collections activity, including customer outreach, dispute coordination, delinquency escalation and business-directed service suspension or reinstatement. TSA Transition & Carve-Out Lead the C2C stand-up for Omni as a newly separated business operating under a Transition Service Agreement (TSA) with its former parent, Thomson Reuters (TR); at Day 1, only Order Entry sits within Omni, with Billing, Cash Application, Collections and Master Data continuing to be delivered by TR under the TSA. Own the TSA exit plan for each C2C function still delivered by TR, partnering with TR and internal stakeholders to agree hard cutover dates and ensure every TR-provided C2C service is replaced, migrated or stood up independently before TSA expiry. Partner with Technology, Finance and Commercial Excellence to sequence system and process separation, minimizing customer and cash-flow disruption throughout the transition. Establish standalone governance, controls and documentation for C2C processes previously reliant on TR systems or shared services, ensuring SOX compliance and audit-readiness across all six Omni New Co legal entities. Provide regular TSA exit status reporting to senior leadership, flagging risks to cutover dates or service continuity. People & Customer Leadership Lead, coach and develop a geographically distributed team across C2C disciplines, creating clear accountability, decision rights and escalation paths. Build team capability as the role expands from Order Entry into Billing, Cash Application, Collections and Master Data, strengthening knowledge transfer and business continuity. Act as a senior point of contact for Sales, Commercial Excellence, Finance and regional business leaders on C2C issues, risks and opportunities. Build a customer-obsessed culture that reduces friction, improves billing accuracy and resolves issues quickly, supporting scalable processes for e Commerce, reseller and B2B/B2C workflows. Provide confident, visible leadership through organizational change, including communications that help transferring employees feel supported and connected to the new business. Governance & Continuous Improvement Establish and monitor service levels, operational KPIs and controls across Order Management, Billing, Cash Application, Collections and Master Data. Track performance metrics such as order turnaround time, invoice accuracy, cash application automation, aged debt and dispute resolution, and ensure quality control over customer and financial transactions. Simplify ways of working, reduce ambiguity around ownership and handoffs, and identify opportunities to automate or standardize manual processes. Partner with Finance and Technology on cash flow, receivables and future-state operating model design beyond the initial TSA exit. About You You're a fit for the role of Director Customer to Cash if your background includes: Significant leadership experience, minimum 15 years in Customer to Cash, Order to Cash, Finance Operations, Shared Services, Billing, Collections, Order Management or related operational functions, including managing managers or multi-site, geographically distributed teams. Proven experience leading Customer to Cash, Order to Cash or Finance Operations through a carve-out, joint venture or divestiture, including operating under a Transition Service Agreement (TSA) with a former parent company. Strong understanding of end-to-end customer, order, invoice, payment, collections and dispute processes in high-volume transactional environments where accuracy and turnaround times are critical. Experience working with enterprise systems such as SAP, Salesforce, Conga, High Radius, Bill Trust, Esker or comparable platforms. Strong process improvement mindset and commercial awareness, including payment terms, credit limits, customer segmentation, e Commerce operations and revenue/cash flow implications. Comfortable operating in a complex, matrixed, ambiguous environment, with excellent communication skills for senior leaders and frontline teams alike. Bachelor's degree in finance, Accounting, Business Administration or a related discipline; a professional qualification (ACCA, CIMA, CPA, CA, CMA) or MBA is a plus. This can include building reports/dashboards within Adobe Analytics utilizing calculated metrics and segments, investigating data quality, solving data anomalies, auditing the websites, producing customer and product funnels, designing tracking strategy for new or updated web experiences, testing to ensure tagging is functioning properly, and serving as a thought leader on topics related to digital commerce, lead generation, and marketing. About the Role In this opportunity as a Senior Digital Analyst, you will: Use web analytics/data to recognize patterns and trends to understand user behavior and identify improvement opportunities. Co-own digital feature wishlist(s) and roadmap with product managers, nurturing strong data-driven decision making; continuously draw insights to drive (or challenge) digital backlog. Partner with marketers and digital product managers to establish measurement plan and then work with developers/platform architects to deploy relevant analytics solutions to ensure right metrics, journeys, and events are captured. Collect business requirements and ask probing questions to fully understand business needs and how it relates to key performance measurements. Develop the analytics, measurement, and tracking strategy for the website and digital campaigns. Produce reports and digital dashboards to track website and campaign performance, business trends, customer behavior and other key success indicators for various operating units and management. Leverage business knowledge and analytical skills to translate complex results into clear insights and recommendations for decision-makers that will support continuous improvement to campaigns and website. Investigate data anomalies to identify root cause and find opportunities for either optimization or clean-up. Share insights and recommendations to digital and marketing leadership through presentations and other communications. Proactively identify ways to improve reporting capabilities that enable bettor or more advanced analysis Serve as Thought Leader. Collaborate with team to ensure consistency of information and reports, share best practices, and develop systems knowledge. Serve as a trusted consultant for digital analytics strategy. Shift Timings: 12 PM to 9 PM (IST). Work from office for 3 days in a week (Mandatory). About You You're a fit for the role of Senior Digital Analyst, if you background includes: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Data Analytics, Economic, Mathematics, Statistics, Finance, Management Information Systems, Computer Science Engineering, or similar data centric disciplines. 6 to 8 years’ experience in marketing or digital analytics roles. 3+ years of hands-on web analytics experience with Adobe Analytics. Experience analyzing digital data including analyses such as customer journey mapping, website flow analysis, audience profiling/segmentation, cohort/mix analysis, digital channel analysis. Understanding of various concepts such as agile/scrum, A/B or multivariate testing, tag management, journey mapping, and segmentation. title: Privacy Engineer - Consent & Enterprise ID
jobDescription:
We are seeking a Privacy Engineer to join our Privacy Technology team. This role will own the full lifecycle of TR’s marketing consent infrastructure — not just cookie banners, but the end-to-end set of controls that determine when and how Thomson Reuters can lawfully target individuals for marketing purposes across our global digital estate. About the

ROLE:
Own the design, configuration, and governance of TR’s marketing consent controls across all digital properties — including preference centers, dynamic web forms, consent banners, and opt-in/opt-out mechanisms for marketing communications. Define and enforce standards for privacy link placement and behavior across TR’s marketing domains, including Do Not Sell/Share links, privacy notices, cookie policy links, and unsubscribe mechanisms. Translate jurisdictional consent requirements (opt-in, opt-out, hybrid) into accurate CMP configurations — geolocation rules, consent categories, banner templates, and script generation for test and production environments. Partner with Marketing, Product and Legal to ensure that any campaign, workflow, or marketing feature that relies on targeting individuals for marketing purposes meets applicable global consent requirements. Own the consent signal chain from collection through to marketing activation — validating that preference and opt-out signals are correctly passed to downstream platforms including CRM, marketing automation, and data platforms. Work closely with the Enterprise Identity function to ensure identity anchors consent signals correctly, including how authenticated user identity is resolved and associated with consent records across channels. Drive the operationalization of TR’s preference center strategy, defining what signals are captured, how they are structured, and how they connect to marketing execution systems. Own TR's domain compliance inventory — the authoritative, multi-team record of the organization's digital estate and its consent, accessibility, and web governance obligations across thousands of properties. Take technical ownership of the automated Python-based domain scanning pipeline: drive it from its current manual cadence to a reliable scheduled production run, maintain detection logic as new consent tools and tracker patterns emerge, coordinate with data engineering on the execution environment and storage pipeline, and govern the shared compliance tracking layer used by Privacy, Accessibility, and Web Operations teams. Lead cookie and tracker categorization and remediation workflows across all TR properties, maintaining the accuracy of the consent inventory as technologies are added or changed, and ensuring new domains are scanned, categorized, and onboarded with correct consent configurations before activation. Support go-live validation for new domains and marketing campaigns requiring consent controls, ensuring mechanisms are correctly implemented before activation. Apply AI tools to automate scanning, categorization, signal validation, and reporting workflows, proactively identifying opportunities to reduce manual effort across the consent program. Contribute to the program’s strategic initiative to establish the CMP as the enterprise system of record for consent and privacy operations, applying marketing consent domain expertise to inform architecture decisions, data models, and integration requirements for the authenticated product scope. About You: 5-7 years of experience in privacy engineering, consent management, or digital compliance. One Trust, Consent Management, GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, Cookie Compliance, Tag Management, Privacy Engineering, Java Script, Python, Data Privacy Google Consent Mode, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Adobe Experience Cloud, Eloqua, Google Tag Manager, Adobe Launch, CASL, Preference Center Management, AI/LLM Tooling, WCAG/Accessibility, SQL, REST APIs, B2B Saa S Hands-on experience with Consent Management Platforms (e.g. One Trust or similar), including preference centers, geolocation rules, and consent category configuration. Working knowledge of GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, CASL, and other global frameworks governing marketing communications and direct targeting. Understanding of the full consent control ecosystem beyond cookies: preference centers, subscription and unsubscribe management, Do Not Sell/Share links, and DSR workflows. Familiarity with how consent signals integrate with marketing technology stacks including CRM, marketing automation, and tag management platforms. Strong attention to detail with the ability to manage compliance across a large portfolio of domains and digital properties. Demonstrated use of AI tools (Microsoft Copilot, Claude Code, or Python-based LLM workflows) to automate compliance tasks such as scanning, categorization, reporting, or gap analysis. Experience designing or operating preference centers or subscription management platforms. Familiarity with marketing technology platforms (Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Eloqua, Adobe Experience Cloud, or similar) and how consent signals are consumed downstream. Understanding of dynamic web form design as a data collection point — privacy-by-design principles, required disclosures, and consent capture at the form level. Experience with tag management systems (Google Tag Manager, Adobe Launch) and consent-based script blocking. Familiarity with Google Consent Mode (v2) — how it integrates with CMP consent signals, its implications for Google Ads and Analytics measurement, and how it is configured in One Trust and tag management environments. Familiarity with privacy link accessibility standards and WCAG requirements for consent interfaces. title: Lead Data Governance & Quality Analyst
jobDescription: Job Requisition: Lead Data Governance & Quality Analyst – Service & Operational Data Location: Bangalore (Hybrid); collaborate with AMERS/EMEA/APAC stakeholders as needed. Job Type: Full-time; Lead-level (hands-on Individual Contributor) We're hiring a Lead Data Governance & Quality Analyst to strengthen how we define, manage, and trust enterprise Service & Operational data across platforms such as Service Now, Datadog, and other IT-related systems. In this role, you'll own governance execution and data quality practices for core Service & Operational domains (e.g., IT Service Management (Incident, Problem, Change, Asset, CMDB, Request, Knowledge, SLAs/SLOs), observability telemetry (metrics, logs, events, synthetics, RUM). Where end-to-end service and operational metrics span multiple systems, you’ll partner partner with Customer Experience and Engineering teams (e.g., Salesforce, Azure Dev Ops) to align cross-domain definitions and quality requirements – driving outcomes through collaboration with business owners, data stewards, product teams, and engineering to ensure data is well-defined, measurable, compliant, and fit for purpose. You'll translate policy into action by establishing clear data definitions, ownership, and measurable controls – implementing data quality rules, monitoring, issue management workflows, and governance operating rhythms that improve decision-making, reduce risk, and enable scalable analytics and AI. About the Role As our Lead Data Governance & Quality Analyst, you will: Lead governance execution for Service & Operational data domains (e.g., Incident/Problem/Change/Request, Observability/Telemetry, Availability/SLA/SLO), ensuring consistent definitions, ownership, and controls. Develop and maintain data quality (DQ) standards: profiling, rule design, thresholds, completeness/accuracy/timeliness checks, and automated monitoring/alerting for priority datasets. Define and maintain data product expectations / contracts (schema, definitions, freshness, SLAs/SLOs, usage guidance) and partner with engineering to implement controls and alerts to ensure compliance. Partner with Data Owners and Stewards to define critical data elements (CDEs), business glossaries, and data product/service expectations (e.g., incident categorization, assignment group, CI mapping, SLA clocks, telemetry tags). Create and manage DQ scorecards and reporting, tying issues to business impact and tracking progress against KPIs; run a regular review cadence with owners/stewards to drive decisions and prioritization. Run data issue management with ITSM-style rigor: intake, triage, severity/priority definitions, root-cause analysis coordination, remediation tracking, and post-fix validation; prevent recurrence via upstream controls and process improvements. Support metadata management: lineage, definitions, classifications, retention, and usage documentation in data catalog tools. Ensure compliance and responsible data use by applying privacy/security classifications (e.g., PII), access controls, and audit-ready documentation. Influence upstream processes (data entry, standards, integrations, reconciliation logic, product changes) to prevent defects and reduce rework (e.g., mandatory fields, controlled vocabularies, CI normalization, tag standards). Contribute to governance operating model: standards, playbooks, training, and change management to increase adoption across teams. Facilitate governance forums (working sessions, steward councils) and drive decisions on definitions, quality thresholds, and prioritization; maintain decision logs and backlog transparency. Partner closely with Service Management, SRE/Observability, Engineering, Data & Analytics teams to align on definitions, controls, and overall plans. About you: To be our Lead Data Governance & Quality Analyst, you will likely have: 5+ years in data governance, data quality, analytics, or related data management roles; experience in a lead capacity strongly preferred, ideally with operational/ITSM/telemetry datasets. Strong knowledge of data governance concepts: data ownership/stewardship, CDEs, metadata, lineage, data lifecycle, and controls – and how they apply to event/ticketing/telemetry data. Advanced SQL skills: comfort analyzing data in relational warehouses/lakes, ability to work with semi-structured data (e.g., JSON/log-like structures) is a plus.
